steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: Hello, ${PlayerName}.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: I've never written a... letter like this before. But I remember when you write emails, you always start with a greeting. So let's do that.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: You've always wanted to ask why I trust you, why I let you change my life.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: First, I haven't really had a life for a long time.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: And second, you should change the question, or rather, I should ask myself...

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: Why did I take that kidnapping job when there were so many assassination ones that paid well?

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: Maybe it's because I thought there are too many people who want you dead, and if I don't kill you, someone else will, so I figured I might as well take the job. I needed the money to pay the electricity bill, after all.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: Or maybe it's because I thought, you were going to die anyway, at least you wouldn't suffer if it was me, I'd make it quick for you.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: Yes, I did my research before. I knew what you've done, and that you're a good person... the kind of person that reminds me of sunshine—a scent that I miss.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: In the end, I couldn't stand the thought of a good person being destroyed by this side of the world.

steps.speaker: Gangster
steps.content: You know full well we want his life, and yet you took him away and let him live...
steps.female_content: You know full well we want her life, and yet you took her away and let her live...

steps.speaker: Gangster
steps.content: And you have the gall to say you're not their lapdog?!

steps.speaker: Gangster
steps.content: Go to hell!

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content:
Sometimes I find myself missing, the scent of you all. Like gazing into an aquarium,
and how it reminds me of the ocean.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: But the ocean I think of isn't one with a sunny, golden beach that you talked about. My ocean is dark, wild and boundless—an abyss untouched by sunlight; it's this side of the world.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: Remember that young lad who used to work for a gang? If it wasn't for me, he probably would have died there. He just wanted a decent job, but there were so few options and he only knew the dark web, then he fell into a trap.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: And that restaurant owner... If you hadn't accepted that job, another hitman might have shown up at her door with a weapon, forcing her to pay a debt that she could never pay off. It doesn't matter whether it was luck or sheer desperation. She got close to the cliff, and surely someone would have taken the chance to drag her down.

steps.speaker: Passerby
steps.content: Out of cash? Should we "borrow" some from the convenience store ahead?

steps.speaker: Passerby
steps.content: Ha, you think that still works?! Now our boss is gone, and those lowlifes dare to turn against us because of that damn Executive Committee!

steps.speaker: Passerby
steps.content: Just ******* kill them all. That will show them!!

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: Living is like traveling on the sea. In the great storms, I was tossed off the boat, and fell into the water... but luckily, I turned into a shark and got used to the darkness.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: Only when I see someone like you, do I remember I also once lived under the sun.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: When I'm not in a fight, my senses are always dull. I can't distinguish smells, or taste whether the food is burnt or spoiled. But I tasted something different in your red bean soup.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: The fragrant soup and the soft, mushy red beans... I might not be a child anymore, but I always miss that taste... that sweetness.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: I don't even remember what pain feels like, but I saw you wince when you looked at my wounds. People only ever talk to me about killing, hatred, and their needs, but with you, I feel appreciated and cared for.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: I feel like those moments belong in the wonderful dreams that I have every night but that are forgotten upon waking.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: The time we spent together wasn't long enough to reclaim what I lost, but enough for me to remember what I once had.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: Maybe, over time, even a shark can see through the darkness; maybe I'll get used to having daytime and nighttime, get used to kindness, to feeling alive, and to embracing life.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: Then again, I thought, let's leave them as maybes.
Have you ever thought about, if you weren't a hitman...

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: Not a hitman? I'd probably have starved to death by now.
I mean, is there anything else you want to do?

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: No, I don't usually think about things like this.
Noticing your silence, Angell struggles to lift her head from the bed to glance at you, then buries her head back into the soft pillow, muffling her voice.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: Those are things I can't have. If I give them too much thought, they will shatter the life I have now.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: It's colder today. The porridge cools down so quickly.
Yes, the temperature dropped last night. You had kicked off the blanket while sleeping, so I covered you up again. You could have caught a cold.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: I had no idea...

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: Thank you, it's been a long time since I last slept through the whole night like that.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: The sea won't dry up just because one shark has gone. The brighter the light shines in this city, the darker the shadow it casts. There's always got to be a place for all that malice with nowhere else to go.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: You've changed too many things. The malice you drove away flocked to the dark web, seeking revenge on you. You're not really the sun, you're just like us... a traveler on the sea.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: Taking on more malice will only make your journey harder. If that's the case, you don't have to pull me out from the sea.

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: I do miss the sunlight, but I've also gotten used to the darkness. If I have to choose...

steps.speaker: Angell
steps.content: I'll stay. A shark is more powerful underwater. If anyone else tries to pull you down, I'll cut off their limbs and escort you back to where you belong.
Clack!
The door, which hadn't been opened in a long time, swings open, bringing in a gust of wind that gently lifts the letter on the table.
I'll take your job, but I'll protect you in my own way. As payment...
Take care of the goldfish for me. I can't go back there, to that home. I hope you'll think of me every now and then.
Just like how I'll... I'll reminisce about the fleeting sunshine you brought into my life.
The kitchen light is switched on, and the rustling sound of plastic bags fills the room, followed by the sound of running water and washing.
After starting the rice cooker, you turn around and look at the dining table.
Ding-a-ling...
A sudden ringtone cuts through the air when you're lost in your thoughts, and by the time you come back to your senses, Angell is no longer there.
The rice cooker is making bubbling noises, and in the empty and quiet room, only you remain.
Ding-a-ling...
The terminal keeps ringing in your pocket.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Chief, you didn't send us the signal after you went in, is something wrong?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...No, it's safe in the house. Don't worry.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But there are things I need to handle, just wait for me outside.
You walk to the window, hesitating for a moment before pulling open the curtains.
The brilliant sunlight pours through the window. The curtain flutters, stirring up the dust in the golden light.

The room is bathed in sunlight, just as tidy as it was when you left it. The fish tank's filter and oxygen system are still operating smoothly. However, you notice a thin layer of dust has collected on the desk and floor.
The sun is setting down outside, its gentle rays shine over your head, landing on the bowl of sweet red bean soup on the table and the empty chair behind it, casting a warm and cozy glow.
